Given data: Number of turns $N = 300$, Relative permeability $\mu_r = 900$, Mean circumference $l = 40\text{ mm} = 40 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$, Cross-sectional area $A = 50\text{ mm}^2 = 50 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$, Current $I = 2.5\text{ A}$.

(i) **Magnetomotive Force (mmf):**
$$\text{mmf} = N \times I = 300 \times 2.5 = 750\text{ AT (Ampere-Turns)}$$

(ii) **Reluctance of the ring ($\mathcal{R}$):**
$$\mathcal{R} = \frac{l}{\mu_0 \mu_r A}$$
where $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ H/m}$.
$$\mathcal{R} = \frac{40 \times 10^{-3}}{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 900 \times (50 \times 10^{-6})}$$
$$\mathcal{R} = \frac{40 \times 10^{-3}}{5.6548 \times 10^{-14}} \approx 7.07 \times 10^{11}\text{ AT/Wb}$$

(iii) **Flux ($\Phi$):**
$$\Phi = \frac{\text{mmf}}{\mathcal{R}} = \frac{750}{7.07 \times 10^{11}} \approx 1.06 \times 10^{-9}\text{ Wb}$$
*(Note: Recalculate with exact denominator: $\Phi = \frac{750 \times 5.6548 \times 10^{-14}}{40 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.06 \times 10^{-9}\text{ Wb}$)*
proTip: Watch out for unit conversions! Always convert millimeters (mm) to meters (m) and square millimeters ($\text{mm}^2$) to square meters ($\text{m}^2$) before calculating magnetic reluctance.
